title: 2025-08-19-pilot-weekly-onboarding-infra-readiness-sync
next_steps: Redwood to share VPC onboarding checklist and security whitepaper by 2025-08-20
LumenTech to provide sample prompt set and expected golden outputs by 2025-08-22
Follow-up POC results review on 2025-08-27 at 15:00 UTC
action_items: Priya Narang - Upload 3 canonical prompt flows + evaluation rubric - 2025-08-22
Aaron McGill - Enable test VPC peering and share connection details - 2025-08-21
Marco Ruiz - Run latency/cold-start microbenchmarks and send raw logs - 2025-08-23
Ava Chen - Send pricing sheet and Dedicated vs Hosted comparison doc - 2025-08-20
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on onboarding progress, VPC access gating, initial benchmark observations, and next steps for a shadow infra test. Customer emphasized data residency and KMS integration; Redwood clarified SSO and audit log options and agreed to run focused latency checks. Action items include prompt set upload, VPC peering details, and benchmark logs.
topics: Next steps and scheduling shadow tests
transcript:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. We're trying to keep this tight — about 45 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Priya (LumenTech): Hi, Priya here. Thanks.
[00:10] Daniel (LumenTech): Daniel on the call.
[00:12] Sophie (LumenTech): Sophie here.
[00:15] Marco (Redwood SE): Marco Ruiz, engineering. Lina from CS will join for notes.
[00:20] Lina (Redwood CSM): Hey team.
[01:05] Ava: Cool. Two quick goals: 1) check onboarding/access status for the private pilot, 2) review the small set of benchmark numbers we ran over the weekend and decide if we need a different test matrix.
[01:22] Priya: Sounds good. Onboarding — we've got the service account created, but the VPC peering is blocked by our security team until Sophie signs off; they had questions about key management.
[01:33] Sophie: Yep. We need to confirm that Redwood can integrate with our AWS KMS and that logs are retained for 12 months. Also want to see SOC 2 evidence.
[01:40] Ava: Totally understood. We'll send our SOC 2 report and KMS integration doc after this. For KMS — Redwood supports customer-managed keys, and the Private control plane can be configured to use your KMS. We'll include details on envelope encryption and key rotation.
[01:58] Sophie: Great. Also, SSO — is SAML supported, and can we map groups for RBAC?
[02:04] Marco: Yes, SAML and OIDC; you can map SAML groups to roles in the console. There is an option to sync with your IDP for automatic role provisioning.
[02:18] Daniel: From infra side, Aaron started the peering request but needs the precise CIDR and the route tables that Redwood expects. Do you have a template?
[02:27] Ava: We do — we'll send the VPC onboarding checklist and the sample route table entries. That'll include the CIDR we recommend and a small NAT/egress pattern.
[02:35] Aaron (LumenTech SRE): (unmuted) Quick question — what about egress controls? We can't allow open internet from the model pool.
[02:42] Marco: Good, that's common. You can restrict egress to our control-plane endpoints or use a NAT with proxy. For on-prem/VPC we support private endpoints so traffic to the model runtime doesn't leave the VPC unless you opt into endpoints.
[02:58] Priya: Ok moving to the benchmarks — you sent a spreadsheet with median latency for our 512-token prompt, correct? We saw a 220ms p95 on the hosted endpoint, which seems optimistic compared to our internal numbers.
[03:10] Ava: Right. The sheet showed a cold-start ~450ms and warm p95 around 220ms for hosted with continuous batching enabled. Marco, can you walk through the setup we used?
[03:20] Marco: Sure. We ran the open-llm-2-13b quantized variant on a single A100 equivalent, sequence length 512, batch windows of 50ms, and a KV cache priming of previous 100 tokens. We also used prefix caching for repeated prompts. One note — the traffic pattern in the test was synthetic and doesn't mimic your tail latency with variable prompt sizes.
[03:45] Daniel: That explains it. Our traffic is spiky with mixed short and long prompts which tends to increase tail latency.
[03:50] Priya: Also, how are you measuring tokenization? We've got some variance because our tokenization pipeline differs slightly.
[03:56] Marco: We tokenized with the same tokenizer version included in our onboarding bundle but there can be off-by-one token differences. We'll share the tokenizer hash.
[04:10] Sophie: Any concerns about model caching or KV cache leaking between tenants? We need strict isolation.
[04:18] Marco: Isolation is enforced per-tenant — KV caches are scoped to the model instance for each customer. We've also got multi-tenancy namespaces. But I hear you about clarifying it in a security doc. We'll add a diagram.
[04:34] Aaron: For the Private deployment, can we bring our own HSM?
[04:38] Ava: Yes, we support HSM/KMS integrations; you'll need to provide the KMIP endpoints. We'll include the HSM integration steps in the doc pack.
[04:50] [05:00] Priya: On the POC goals — our success criteria are threefold: latency p95 under 350ms for 256-token prompts, cost per 1k tokens below $0.60 in the pilot, and no data egress outside our VPC.
[05:16] Ava: Noted. Those are actionable. We'll focus the next microbench on 256 tokens with your traffic-shaped distribution.
[05:30] Marco: Question for Priya — can you share the distribution? Like percent short (<64 tokens), medium (64-256), long (256+)?
[05:37] Priya: Roughly 40% short, 45% medium, 15% long. We'll upload a sample trace.
[05:44] Ava: Perfect. That'll help tune batching parameters — we can recommend dynamic batch windows to keep p95 low.
[06:00] Daniel: The dedicated vs hosted conversation — we have a budget constraint and want to understand cost delta if we go Dedicated for predictability. Ava, can you give a top-level?
[06:12] Ava: Yes — Dedicated has higher fixed monthly commit but usually lower per-token unit when you amortize over steady usage. Hosted is operationally simpler and has lower start-up. We'll send a Dedicated vs Hosted TCO example using your projected qps.
[06:30] Priya: Also curious about quantization impact on quality; we can't drop below a certain accuracy for our reranking flows.
[06:36] Marco: We'll run an A/B with 4-bit and 8-bit quantized variants against your golden set. Expect small precision delta on generation quality, but for reranking often quantization is less impactful because the scoring head has less sensitivity — though we should validate.
[06:55] Sophie: On compliance, do you have audit logs that show model version and request IDs for each inference? That's required for our GDPR / audit trails.
[07:04] Marco: Audit logs include request ID, model version, input hash, and response metadata. We can retain logs per your retention policy; retention is configurable. We'll include sample log schema.
[07:20] Priya: Great. Back to access — we're blocked waiting on Sophie sign-off; Sophie, main outstanding for you?
[07:26] Sophie: KMS integration details and proof around no data exfiltration during inference. If you can provide network diagrams and the envelope encryption explanation I'm comfortable to approve peering for a test VPC.
[07:39] Ava: We'll email the diagram and the KMS flow today.
[07:45] [08:00] Marco: Quick note on the microbench plan: we'll run three runs — cold-start, steady-state with batching, and spiky pattern with mixed prompt sizes. Expect artifacts: p50/p95, cpu/gpu utilization, and token cost estimates. We'll share raw logs for your infra team to ingest.
[08:20] Aaron: Perfect. For the raw logs, what's the format? JSON lines?
[08:24] Marco: JSONL, with timestamps and GPU counters. We'll redact any PII.
[08:30] Priya: Any plan for causal cache warm-ups? For our workload we see big improvements if the KV cache is primed by prior prompts in a session.
[08:38] Marco: We can simulate session affinity in the pilot and measure delta. We'll include a priming scenario.
[09:00] [10:01] Daniel: On networking, do you require BGP or is static peering enough for the pilot?
[10:08] Ava: Static peering is fine for the pilot; BGP for production at scale is supported but not necessary now.
[10:20] Sophie: One more policy question — can we redact user PII at the edge before sending to Redwood? We want to do that for the first phase.
[10:29] Marco: Absolutely. You can run a small preprocessor to redact or hash sensitive fields. That aligns with typical implementations. We'll add a sample preprocessor snippet to the repo.
[10:45] Priya: Ok moving to the preliminary numbers — Marco, you sent p95 220ms but in our quick internal run we saw p95 ~600ms for similar payloads. What do you think causes that discrepancy?
[11:02] Marco: A few likely causes: tokenization mismatch, traffic shaping, instance type differences, and warm vs cold conditions. Also if you have network egress proxies that add latency.
[11:22] Aaron: We do have an egress proxy chain for auditing, which adds ~80-120ms per request. That matters.
[11:30] Priya: So realistic target is maybe 350-450ms with our stack; ok let's set the p95 goal to 450ms for the pilot then revisit.
[11:39] Ava: Sounds reasonable. We'll run the bench that includes your egress proxy in the loop to match your path.
[12:00] [13:00] (small side conversation; inaudible)
[14:00] Marco: On instrumentation — we'll include tracing headers so you can correlate request IDs end-to-end. Is your tracing stack Jaeger?
[14:08] Daniel: We use Tempo and Honeycomb for traces.
[14:12] Marco: We'll export compatible spans and correlate by request ID.
[15:00] Priya: For the golden outputs — do you want raw outputs or normalized diffs?
[15:06] Marco: Normalized diffs are best for automated scoring, but send both if easy.
[15:20] Sophie: Can Redwood guarantee that model weights aren't copied into logs or external telemetry? That's a security check.
[15:28] Marco: We do not export model weights; logs contain only metadata and request/response hashes if you enable them. We'll call out the log schema again in the security pack.
[16:00] Ava: Quick reconciliation on timeline: If we get prompts by Friday (8/22) and VPC peering details by 8/21, Marco can run microbenches and ship results by 8/23, then we meet 8/27 to review. Is that ok?
[16:20] Priya: Yes.
[16:25] Aaron: Yes, pending Sophie's sign-off on KMS.
[16:30] Sophie: I'll aim to review docs by 8/20.
[16:40] [18:00] Priya: Any blockers from Redwood side for the shadow test?
[18:06] Marco: No blockers. We'll need the peering details and sample traces.
[18:15] Ava: We'll send the onboarding checklist and the SOC2 doc today. Also the Dedicated vs Hosted TCO by tomorrow.
[19:00] (overlap) Daniel: Can we also get an explicit call-out about data residency — where logs live for Private deployment?
[19:07] Marco: Logs are stored in your VPC, or we can ship them to customer S3 if you prefer; retention controls remain with you.
[19:20] Priya: Ok good.
[20:00] Ava: Alright let's do a quick recap of action items and owners...
[20:06] Ava: Priya — upload prompt flows + rubric by 8/22.
[20:10] Ava: Aaron — VPC peering, CIDR and route tables by 8/21.
[20:14] Ava: Marco — run microbenches with your traffic shape and share JSONL logs by 8/23.
[20:18] Ava: Lina — send calendar invite for 8/27 results review.
[20:22] Lina: Sending now.
[20:28] Sophie: One last question — pricing? Are pilot discounts available?
[20:33] Ava: For pilots we can extend a temporary usage credit and discounted unit pricing for the first 3 months; I'll include specifics in the pricing sheet.
[20:40] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[20:45] Marco: Thanks all.
[20:50] [21:00] (meeting ends)
questions: Can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS and HSM?
What is the expected p95 latency under our egress proxy?
How is KV cache isolation enforced between tenants?
Will Redwood provide SOC2 and audit log schemas?
